_meta.description: Endgame principles and patterns — position-type based rules
_meta.match_strategy: Material count + piece configuration on the board

king_and_pawn_opposition.name: King and Pawn — Opposition
king_and_pawn_opposition.key_rule: The attacking king must get in FRONT of the pawn to win.
king_and_pawn_opposition.explanation: With king and pawn vs king, the attacker wins only if their king reaches the 6th rank in front of the pawn.
king_and_pawn_opposition.common_mistake: Pushing the pawn before the king is in front
king_and_pawn_opposition.correct_technique: Use the king to gain opposition, then advance the pawn
king_and_pawn_opposition.rule: King in FRONT of the pawn wins. King BEHIND the pawn draws.

king_and_pawn_key_squares.name: King and Pawn — Key Squares
king_and_pawn_key_squares.key_rule: Each pawn has key squares. If your king reaches them, you win.
king_and_pawn_key_squares.explanation: Key squares are the three squares two ranks ahead of the pawn. If your king occupies any of them, the pawn promotes.
king_and_pawn_key_squares.common_mistake: Not knowing which squares guarantee promotion
king_and_pawn_key_squares.correct_technique: Learn the key squares for each pawn file — they determine the win/draw boundary
king_and_pawn_key_squares.rule: Learn the key squares for your pawn. King on a key square = guaranteed promotion.

rook_endgame_activity.name: Rook Endgames — Rook Activity
rook_endgame_activity.key_rule: Rook activity is more important than material.
rook_endgame_activity.explanation: In rook endgames, an active rook on the 7th rank is often worth more than a pawn.
rook_endgame_activity.correct_technique: Activate your rook even if it costs a pawn
rook_endgame_activity.rule: Active rook > extra pawn. Get your rook to the 7th rank.

rook_behind_passed_pawn.name: Rook Endgames — Rook Behind Passed Pawn
rook_behind_passed_pawn.key_rule: Place your rook BEHIND passed pawns (yours or opponent's).
rook_behind_passed_pawn.explanation: A rook behind a passed pawn gains activity as the pawn advances. A rook in front loses activity.
rook_behind_passed_pawn.common_mistake: Putting rook in front of passed pawn
rook_behind_passed_pawn.correct_technique: Rook behind your passed pawn to support. Rook behind opponent's to stop it.
rook_behind_passed_pawn.rule: Rooks belong BEHIND passed pawns, never in front.

lucena_position.name: Lucena Position — Building a Bridge
lucena_position.key_rule: Win by building a bridge with your rook.
lucena_position.explanation: With rook and pawn on the 7th rank and enemy king cut off, use your rook to block checks.
lucena_position.common_mistake: Trying to promote immediately without the bridge
lucena_position.correct_technique: Rook to the 4th rank, then use it to shield the king from checks
lucena_position.rule: Lucena: Build the bridge. Rook to 4th rank, then shield the king.

philidor_position.name: Philidor Position — Third Rank Defense
philidor_position.key_rule: Defend by keeping your rook on the 3rd rank until the pawn advances.
philidor_position.explanation: With rook and pawn vs rook, the defender draws by keeping their rook on the 3rd rank.
philidor_position.common_mistake: Going to the back rank too early
philidor_position.correct_technique: Stay on 3rd rank. Only go to back rank when pawn reaches 6th.
philidor_position.rule: Philidor defense: 3rd rank until pawn advances, then back rank for checks.

rook_endgame_cut_off_king.name: Rook Endgames — Cutting Off the King
rook_endgame_cut_off_king.key_rule: Cut the enemy king off from the passed pawn with your rook.
rook_endgame_cut_off_king.explanation: The further the enemy king is cut off from the pawn, the easier it is to promote.
rook_endgame_cut_off_king.common_mistake: Not using the rook to create a barrier between the enemy king and pawn
rook_endgame_cut_off_king.correct_technique: Place rook on a file or rank that blocks the enemy king from approaching your pawn
rook_endgame_cut_off_king.rule: Cut off the king with your rook. Every file of distance makes the pawn harder to stop.

opposite_bishops_draw.name: Opposite Colored Bishops — Drawing Tendency
opposite_bishops_draw.key_rule: Opposite colored bishops favor the defender.
opposite_bishops_draw.explanation: With opposite colored bishops, even a 2-pawn advantage may not be enough to win.
opposite_bishops_draw.correct_technique: Place pawns on squares your bishop controls, blockade on enemy bishop color
opposite_bishops_draw.rule: Opposite bishops: defense has huge drawing chances. Don't trade into this if you're winning!

same_color_bishops_technique.name: Same Colored Bishops — Active Bishop Wins
same_color_bishops_technique.key_rule: The bishop that controls more space usually wins.
same_color_bishops_technique.explanation: In same-colored bishop endings, the active bishop dominates. Place pawns on opposite color.
same_color_bishops_technique.common_mistake: Placing pawns on the same color as your bishop, restricting it
same_color_bishops_technique.correct_technique: Put pawns on the opposite color from your bishop so it has maximum scope
same_color_bishops_technique.rule: Put your pawns on the OPPOSITE color of your bishop. Keep the bishop's diagonals open.

knight_vs_bishop_endgame.name: Knight vs Bishop — Pawn Structure Matters
knight_vs_bishop_endgame.key_rule: Knight prefers closed positions, bishop prefers open positions.
knight_vs_bishop_endgame.explanation: Knights are better with locked pawns. Bishops are better in open positions with pawns on both sides.
knight_vs_bishop_endgame.common_mistake: Not considering pawn structure when trading pieces
knight_vs_bishop_endgame.correct_technique: Trade into knight endgame if position is closed. Trade into bishop endgame if open.
knight_vs_bishop_endgame.rule: Knight = closed positions. Bishop = open positions with pawns on both sides.

knight_endgame_outpost.name: Knight Endgames — Central Outpost
knight_endgame_outpost.key_rule: A knight on an outpost in the center dominates the endgame.
knight_endgame_outpost.explanation: A knight on a protected central square (d5, e5, d4, e4) that can't be challenged by pawns is a monster.
knight_endgame_outpost.common_mistake: Trading the knight when it's on a strong outpost
knight_endgame_outpost.correct_technique: Plant the knight on an outpost and use it as a launching pad for the king march
knight_endgame_outpost.rule: A knight on an outpost is worth a rook in the endgame. Never trade it voluntarily.

queen_endgame_checks.name: Queen Endgames — Perpetual Check Drawing
queen_endgame_checks.key_rule: Queen endgames are very drawish due to perpetual checks.
queen_endgame_checks.explanation: Queens are the best piece for giving perpetual checks. If you're behind, look for perpetual.
queen_endgame_checks.common_mistake: Assuming a pawn up with queens on the board is winning
queen_endgame_checks.correct_technique: When behind, look for perpetual check. When ahead, shelter your king before pushing pawns.
queen_endgame_checks.rule: Queen endgames: pawn up often draws. Always check for perpetual before playing on.

two_bishops_advantage.name: Two Bishops — Bishop Pair Advantage
two_bishops_advantage.key_rule: The two bishops are strong in open positions.
two_bishops_advantage.explanation: Two bishops work together to control both color complexes. In open positions, they dominate knights.
two_bishops_advantage.common_mistake: Trading a bishop unnecessarily, giving up the bishop pair
two_bishops_advantage.correct_technique: Keep the bishop pair, open the position, and use them to dominate the diagonals
two_bishops_advantage.rule: Two bishops beat two knights in open positions. Protect your bishop pair.

wrong_bishop_rook_pawn.name: Wrong Bishop + Rook Pawn — Fortress Draw
wrong_bishop_rook_pawn.key_rule: A bishop that doesn't control the promotion square of a rook pawn = draw.
wrong_bishop_rook_pawn.explanation: If your bishop doesn't control the corner square where the rook pawn promotes (a8/h8), the enemy king just sits in the corner.
wrong_bishop_rook_pawn.common_mistake: Playing for a win when you have the wrong bishop
wrong_bishop_rook_pawn.correct_technique: If you have the wrong bishop, don't trade all the pawns. Keep pawns on both sides.
wrong_bishop_rook_pawn.rule: Wrong bishop + rook pawn = draw. The enemy king sits in the corner and you can't get it out.

king_activity_endgame.name: General Endgame — King Activity
king_activity_endgame.key_rule: In the endgame, the king is a fighting piece.
king_activity_endgame.explanation: Once queens are off the board, centralize your king immediately. A centralized king is worth a piece.
king_activity_endgame.common_mistake: Leaving the king on the back rank in the endgame
king_activity_endgame.correct_technique: March your king to the center (d4/e4/d5/e5) as soon as the queens come off
king_activity_endgame.rule: Centralize the king in endgames. A king on e4 is worth half a piece.

passed_pawn_creation.name: General Endgame — Creating Passed Pawns
passed_pawn_creation.key_rule: A passed pawn is the most valuable asset in the endgame.
passed_pawn_creation.explanation: A passed pawn (no opposing pawns blocking or guarding its advance) ties down enemy pieces.
passed_pawn_creation.common_mistake: Not creating passed pawns when you have a pawn majority
passed_pawn_creation.correct_technique: Use your pawn majority to create a passed pawn. Push the candidate pawn forward.
passed_pawn_creation.rule: Create a passed pawn from your pawn majority. It ties down your opponent's pieces.

outside_passed_pawn.name: General Endgame — Outside Passed Pawn
outside_passed_pawn.key_rule: An outside passed pawn wins by distracting the enemy king.
outside_passed_pawn.explanation: An outside passed pawn (far from the remaining pawns) forces the enemy king to run to stop it, leaving the other pawns undefended.
outside_passed_pawn.common_mistake: Not recognizing the power of a distant passed pawn
outside_passed_pawn.correct_technique: Push the outside passed pawn, force the king to chase it, then capture the remaining pawns with your king
outside_passed_pawn.rule: Outside passed pawn = decoy. Push it, distract the king, win the other pawns.
